classification_signals: No explicit methods section detailing participants, data collection, or statistical analysis.
The paper synthesizes existing research and observations (e.g., 'Numerous studies... have been conducted by foreign researchers', 'Researchers write about non-boring design').
It presents a conceptual model (Table 1. Stages of dynamics by age) and discusses its implications without presenting new empirical data to support it.

The conclusion identifies a research gap ('almost no researchers who have studied the impact of the interior on the human psyche in relation to the dynamics of human age'), typical of review articles.
The abstract mentions 'recommendations of Uzbek researchers' and 'projects and recommendations applied', suggesting a synthesis of local expertise and practice rather than a new empirical study.
title: The Influence Of Interior Psychology On Uzbek Architecture

findings.antecedent: non-boring design (combination of style, decorative motifs, novelty, antiquity, craftsmanship, high-tech, real antiques, avant-garde furniture)
findings.consequent: popularity among designers; designers' tendency to create personal mixes and search for rare, structured items with good names
findings.quote: The combination of style and decorative motifs, novelty and antiquity... is extremely popular among designers... Any self-respecting professional will try to create their own personal mix...

findings.antecedent: colours (mystery, symbols, attachment to the universe)
findings.quote: The mystery of the world of colours... have always fascinated people. Experts... have captured everyone's attention and interest with their knowledge of the magical world of colours [1,2].
Colour always affects a person. It affects his physical and mental condition.

findings.consequent: formation of specific feelings, images, and emotions
findings.quote: Having an understanding of colours, it is possible to form specific feelings and images that evoke certain emotions.

findings.consequent: artistic quality of the interior; favourable conditions for human life, activity, health, and mood
findings.quote: Colours not only enhance the artistic quality of the interior... but also help to create favourable conditions for human life and activity, health and mood [3,4].

findings.antecedent: interior design features for children aged 3-7 (bright colour, differentiated form of objects/interiors)
findings.quote: In the first stage with the central attributes, bright colour and differentiated form for the resulting reconstruction as an object... The child 'feels too late' for other attributes.
their preferences are largely determined by their parents... child's feelings, inner experiences begin to manifest themselves in a unique, individual way [5,6,7].

findings.antecedent: small mistake in interior design (colours, fixtures, design) for adolescents (12-17 years old)
findings.quote: a small mistake in the design of the interior... can have a negative impact on the child's psychology.

findings.consequent: individual's ability to participate in interior design process; ability to determine colour, light, object location according to nature
findings.quote: At this stage, the owners will... be able to participate in the process themselves. Man can determine the colour, light, location of objects according to his nature.

findings.consequent: quality of preference for interiors (changes, not quantity); preferences determined by social roles, situations, age, physiological peculiarities, fashions; ability to independently participate in interior design and give advice from a psychological point of view
findings.quote: there will be a change in the quality of preference [8,9]. It is determined by the social roles performed... Young owners at this stage will now be able to independently participate in the interior design...

findings.consequent: consumer preference for interiors (decrease in qualitative aspects, dissociation of purchasing/user preference, less new advantage for self, consistency in style, increased importance of price/brand)
findings.quote: This stage is characterized by the appearance of a decrease in consumer preference... a new dissociation... goods of the same type and style are used... leading attribute is the price and structure of the brand.
The importance of human age in the attractiveness of modern interiors is incomparable.

findings.consequent: preference for interiors (different looks, colours, furnishings)
findings.quote: People of all ages like interiors of different looks, colours, and different furnishings.

limitations: There are almost no researchers who have studied the impact of the interior on the human psyche in relation to the dynamics of human age.
minimum_safe_summary: This narrative review by Qosimov and Urmonov (2021) explores the influence of interior psychology on Uzbek architecture, focusing on how human age impacts preferences and needs in modern interiors. The paper synthesizes existing research on color psychology and design trends, proposing a six-stage model of age-related psychological development and its implications for interior design choices, from childhood to middle age. Key findings suggest that preferences for design elements like bright colors and differentiated forms are prominent in early childhood, while adolescent preferences are influenced by both parents and peer groups, with design mistakes potentially impacting their psychology. As individuals mature, their autonomy in design decisions increases, and preferences shift from quantitative to qualitative, eventually prioritizing factors like price and brand in later stages. The authors highlight a research gap concerning the specific impact of interior design on the human psyche across different age dynamics.
